roles.name: Owner
roles.description: The billing and legal owner of the tenant; holds every permission in the catalogue including the ones that can destroy the tenant itself. Exists so that there is always exactly one accountable human who can re-grant access after everyone else has locked themselves out.

roles.name: Admin
roles.description: Runs the workspace day to day: invites users, assigns roles of lower rank, configures integrations and reads every module. Deliberately holds no payroll approval by default, so that IT administration and money movement are not the same job.

roles.name: Accountant
roles.description: Owns the general ledger, the sales and purchase sub-ledgers, banking and the fiscal calendar; posts, voids, reverses and closes periods. Explicitly excluded from `payroll.payroll_run.approve` so the person who calculates a payroll run is never the person who releases the money.

roles.name: HR Manager
roles.description: Owns the employee master file, the org chart, leave policy and the payroll cycle up to and including approval. Sees compensation data for the whole tenant but has no access to the ledger, so HR cannot post an adjusting entry to hide a payroll error.

roles.name: Department Manager
roles.description: A line manager who approves the work and absence of the department subtree they own, and reads the operational data of that subtree only. Their authority is defined almost entirely by ABAC scope rather than by permission grants, which is why one role covers every department.

roles.name: Read-Only Auditor
roles.description: An external or internal reviewer granted time-boxed read access to the books, reports and audit log via `RoleAssignment.valid_until`. Holds no permission whose action mutates state, and is denied credential-surface reads (`api_key`, `gateway_config`) because an auditor never needs them.

roles.name: Employee
roles.description: The self-service role every staff member with a login receives: their own payslips, leave, attendance, expenses, timesheets and profile. Every grant is paired with an `own_record` scope, so the RBAC layer and the ABAC layer would both have to fail before one employee saw another's pay.
